lines.say: [gently] Toby? It's late. Why aren't you home?
[sniffling] I spent Dad's money on candied figs.
cap: I spent Dad's money on {o:candied figs}.

lines.say: [amused] How much of it?
[wailing] ALL OF IT!
[warmly] Jesus once told a story about a son who did way worse.
cap: about a son who did way worse.

lines.say: [storytelling] A man had two sons.
[arrogant] Father. Give me my share of the inheritance. Now.
cap: “Father. Give me my share of the inheritance.

lines.say: [confused] Wait... don't you only get that when your dad... dies?
cap: Wait... don't you only get that

lines.say: [softly] Exactly. It was like saying: I wish you were gone.
cap: It was like saying: {r:I wish you were gone.}

lines.say: [sadly] And the father... gave it to him.
So the son left for a far country... and wasted every coin. Parties. Friends. Fancy everything.
cap: So the son left for a far country...

lines.say: [ominous] Then the money ran out. A famine hit. And his friends... were gone.
cap: Then the money ran out. A {r:famine} hit.

lines.say: The only job he could find... was feeding pigs.
cap: The only job he could find...

lines.say: [disgusted] PIGS?!
[sadly] He was so hungry... he wanted to eat what the pigs were eating.
cap: he wanted to eat what the {o:pigs} were eating.

lines.say: [softly] And then... he came to his senses.
[broken] My father's servants have more than enough bread... and I'm starving. I'll go back. I'll say I'm not worthy to be his son. Just make me a servant.
cap: “My father's servants have more than enough bread...
I'll say I'm not worthy to be his son.

lines.say: So he started the long walk home... rehearsing his speech the whole way.
cap: So he started the long walk {g:home}...
rehearsing his speech the whole way.

lines.say: [slowly] But while he was still a long way off...
cap: But while he was still a {o:long way off}...

lines.say: [emotional] his father saw him.
Back then, a respected old man never ran. It was undignified.
cap: Back then, a respected old man {r:never ran}.

lines.say: [building, emotional] He ran anyway.
[whispers] He RAN?
[emotional] He threw his arms around his son... and kissed him.
cap: He threw his arms around his son...

lines.say: [crying] Father... I have sinned against heaven and against you. I'm not worthy to be called your son...
cap: “Father... I have sinned against heaven and against you.
I'm not worthy to be called your son...”

lines.say: [smiling] He never even got to finish the speech.
cap: He never even got to {g:finish the speech}.

lines.say: [joyful] [shouting] Quick! Bring the best robe! Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet! We're going to celebrate!
cap: A {g:ring} for his hand! Sandals for his feet!

lines.say: [emotional] This son of mine was dead... and is alive again. He was lost... and is found!
cap: “This son of mine was dead... and is {g:alive} again.

lines.say: [quietly] But someone wasn't celebrating. The older brother. The one who never left.
[bitter] [angry] All these years I've slaved for you, and you never gave me so much as a goat to party with my friends!
cap: “All these years I've slaved for you...
and you never gave me so much as a {r:goat}!”

lines.say: [gently] My son... you are always with me. And everything I have is yours.
cap: “My son... you are always with me.

lines.say: [softly] Jesus ended the story right there. The older brother still outside... deciding whether to come in.
cap: Jesus ended the story right there.

lines.say: [softly] So... both sons were lost.
[warmly] One ran away. One stayed... and still didn't get it. And the father went out to both of them.
cap: One stayed... and still didn't get it.
And the father went out to {g:both of them}.

lines.say: [tenderly] That's what God is like, Toby. No matter how far you've gone... He's already running toward you.
cap: No matter how far you've gone...

lines.say: [hopeful] ...Do you think Dad will run?
[warmly] Only one way to find out.
